Peppol e-invoicing (BIS Billing 3.0)

Sends customer invoices and credit notes as Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 e-invoices, turns received e-invoices into draft vendor bills and handles business responses — through whichever EDI provider is installed.

Version19.0.1.7.1
EditionCommunity and Enterprise
LicenceAGPL-3
Requiresedi_base, account_edi_ubl_cii
Extended byedi_editel_peppol, edi_epostak_peppol, edi_grit_peppol

What it is for

Peppol is the European network for exchanging electronic invoices. A company joins it through an access point (a Peppol service provider) and is found on it by its Peppol address — a scheme code plus an identifier, for example 0245:2020123456 for a Slovak company identified by its DIČ. The invoice itself is a Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 file: UBL 2.1 XML that follows the European standard EN 16931.

This module does everything about the document and nothing about the transport:

  • decides, for every customer invoice and credit note, whether it goes out as an e-invoice or as a PDF, and says why (routing);
  • generates the BIS 3.0 file with Odoo's own builder and hands it to the installed provider (sending);
  • shows what happened to it (statuses);
  • turns received e-invoices and credit notes into draft vendor bills (receiving);
  • records the responses your customers send back and lets you answer your suppliers (responses).

The transport — the connection to an access point — comes from a provider module:

Access point Module
ePošťák edi_epostak_peppol
Editel eXite edi_editel_peppol
GRiT Orion edi_grit_peppol

It does not use Odoo's own Peppol service (account_peppol). If that is installed too, the two never send the same invoice: see routing.

For Slovak invoices, install l10n_sk_ubl_bis3 as well. It identifies Slovak parties by their DIČ and puts the variable symbol into the file where the payer's bank looks for it; this module uses its builder automatically.

Legal background

Slovakia. All references are to the VAT Act.

  • Until 31 December 2026 an electronic invoice may be issued only with the recipient's consent — § 71 ods. 1 písm. b). For 2026 alone, § 85o ods. 21 and 22 waive that consent for an invoice in the European standard's data structure sent through a delivery service (doručovacia služba) to a business established in Slovakia that can receive it that way — except for supplies exempt under § 28 to § 43 and § 47 and for simplified invoices.
  • From 1 January 2027 e-invoicing is mandatory. Under § 85o ods. 2 and 3 in the wording effective from that day, a VAT payer that supplies goods or services with the place of supply in Slovakia to a taxable person established in Slovakia, or to a non-taxable legal person established there, or receives a payment before such a supply, must issue an electronic invoice; exempt supplies (§ 28 to § 43 and § 47) and simplified invoices are excluded. Issuing it needs no consent; sending it other than through a delivery service does. Under ods. 4 an electronic invoice is a document with the particulars of § 74 ods. 1 in a format allowing automated processing and in a data structure that follows the European standard for electronic invoicing. A document changing it must be an electronic invoice too, quote the original's number and travel the same way (ods. 5), and the invoice must be issued within fifteen days (ods. 6). The invoice data are reported to the Financial Directorate through the delivery service, and handing the invoice to the delivery service fulfils that duty (ods. 9 to 11). E-invoices are kept for ten years (ods. 15). The same amendment adds § 71 ods. 5: whoever must issue e-invoices must be able to send and receive them through a delivery service, and every domestic recipient of such supplies must be able to receive them. These provisions are not yet in the consolidated text in force today; the link leads to § 85o as it stands now. By § 85o ods. 1 this regime is transitional, from 1 January 2027 to 30 June 2030.
  • The delivery service is provided by a certified provider entered in the register kept by the Financial Directorate (§ 76a). Whether your access point is such a provider is a question for the provider, not for Odoo.

Czech Republic. There is no general e-invoicing mandate. A tax document may be electronic only if the customer agrees — § 26 odst. 3 of the VAT Act. The Czech national format ISDOC is described in account_edi_isdoc.

European Union. Directive 2014/55/EU on electronic invoicing in public procurement requires public contracting authorities to receive and process invoices that comply with the European standard on electronic invoicing (EN 16931) and one of its listed syntaxes (Article 7). Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is a specification of EN 16931 in the UBL syntax.

Setting it up

  1. Install and connect a provider, for example ePošťák.
  2. Company settings. Settings → EDI, block Peppol BIS3 (this company). Every setting belongs to the company you are working in, so a Slovak company can e-invoice while its Czech sister does not:
Setting What it does
Allow e-invoicing via Peppol A permission, not a routing decision. Off: no customer invoice or credit note of this company leaves through Peppol, whatever a contact says. Receiving is not affected.
Peppol scope For contacts that state no preference: Slovak mandate: domestic B2B and B2G only, or Any customer with a Peppol address (default). See routing.
Auto-send Peppol on Invoice Post Every posted document routed to Peppol is generated and queued at once. Off: use Send via Peppol or Send.
Peppol Purchase Journal Journal for received e-invoices. Empty: the company's first purchase journal.

Peppol Transport in the same block (database-wide) chooses which provider carries the documents when more than one is installed. It must be set then: with several installed and none chosen, nothing goes through Peppol and every invoice shows blocked with that reason. With a single provider it does not matter. 3. Your company's Peppol address. On your company's contact, tab Invoicing, group Customer Invoices: Peppol e-address (EAS) and the endpoint next to it. A Slovak company uses scheme 0245 with its DIČ (ten digits) — not the IČ DPH (scheme 9950) and not the IČO; see the Slovak Peppol identifier. 4. Each customer's and supplier's Peppol address, in the same place. 5. Invoice sending on a contact (same group; Odoo normally hides it outside developer mode, this module shows it) says how that customer receives invoices. Choose by e-invoice (Peppol) to send every invoice of that customer through Peppol regardless of the scope. If the company works under the Slovak mandate and a Slovak business is set to anything else, the contact shows a warning that from 1. 1. 2027 its invoices must be e-invoices. 6. Access. The Send via Peppol and Peppol Response… buttons are shown to the EDI User group. Anyone who may edit the invoice can send it: posting with Auto-send on and Send & Print need no EDI group, and the EDI message is recorded on the user's behalf.

E-invoice or PDF

Every customer invoice and credit note shows how it goes out: a badge in the form header once posted, and Sent as with Why at the top of the Other Info tab.

Sent as Meaning
Peppol e-invoice goes out through Peppol
PDF goes out the usual way (email, print); Peppol does not apply
Peppol, but blocked should go through Peppol but cannot: a Peppol address is missing

The decision, in this order:

  1. The company does not allow e-invoicing → PDF.
  2. The contact's Invoice sending is by e-invoice (Peppol) → Peppol, or blocked if your company or the customer has no Peppol address.
  3. It is Peppol — Odoo's own Peppol service → PDF as far as this module is concerned; Odoo's service sends it, so the invoice never leaves through two access points.
  4. It is anything else, for example by Email → PDF.
  5. Nothing is chosen on the contact, and the scope is the Slovak mandate: a company whose fiscal country is not Slovakia or that has no VAT number (not a VAT payer), a customer outside Slovakia, or a customer with no business identifier at all — not a company and without a VAT number, IČO or DIČ (treated as a consumer) → PDF. A sole trader with an IČO but no VAT number is a business: the mandate covers every taxable person. So is an invoice whose every line is an exempt supply (its taxes are exempt or outside VAT, see below) → PDF.
  6. Your company has no Peppol address → blocked. The customer has none → blocked under the Slovak mandate, PDF under any customer with a Peppol address.
  7. Several Peppol transports are installed and Peppol Transport names none → blocked.
  8. Otherwise → Peppol.

The rule for the Slovak mandate follows § 85o ods. 2 and 3 as far as the data of a contact allow: a VAT payer supplying a taxable person (any business, VAT-registered or not) or a non-taxable legal person established in Slovakia. An exempt supply (§ 28 to § 43, § 47) is left out by the taxes on the invoice: when every line's taxes are exempt (UBL category E) or outside VAT (O), the invoice goes as a PDF. One taxable line, or a line with no tax at all, keeps it in. A reverse-charge sale tax you create yourself needs the Reverse charge flag or category AE, or it reads as exempt. A domestic reverse charge (§ 69 ods. 12) is taxable and stays in, though it is 0 % too. The place of supply is not looked at. Simplified invoices are receipts, which are never sent. Where the law gives a different answer for a customer, set Invoice sending on that contact.

Sending

A posted document routed to Peppol is sent in one of three ways:

  • Automatically on posting, if Auto-send Peppol on Invoice Post is on. An invoice that would have gone but is blocked gets a chatter line "Not sent via Peppol: …" with the reason; one whose file fails Odoo's checks gets the same line with the errors and a Peppol e-invoice not sent activity for its salesperson. The invoice stays posted.
  • Send via Peppol in the form header.
  • Send (Odoo's Send dialog). The method by e-invoice (Peppol) is offered and ticked; when the contact has no Invoice sending chosen it replaces the email default, and Odoo's own Peppol method is unticked. A failure is shown in the dialog as "The e-invoice could not be sent". A document already queued or sent is skipped.

Sending generates the BIS 3.0 file with the builder of the customer's eInvoice format if that is a Peppol format, otherwise with the format Odoo suggests for the customer — for a Slovak customer with l10n_sk_ubl_bis3 installed, the Slovak one. If Odoo's checks of the EN 16931 and Peppol rules fail, nothing is sent and the errors are listed. Otherwise an outbound EDI message is created, the file stored on it, the message queued at the provider and a chatter line written: "Invoice sent via Peppol: … (queued)".

Each document has one outbound message. Sending again reuses it with a freshly generated file, through the transport and in the test or production mode in force now — a document first tried in a test environment goes to production once you have switched. While that message is Queued or Sent, sending again is refused ("already being sent"); once it is Done in production, too ("already delivered"): a delivered invoice is corrected with a credit note, not sent twice.

Statuses

On the invoice:

Field Shows
Peppol Status the state of the latest outbound message: Ready, Queued, Sent, Error, Done (see states)
Peppol Delivery Response the latest message-level response (MLR) from the network, as "code — description"
Peppol Invoice Response the customer's latest business response, for example Accepted or Rejected
Peppol Response Reason the reason the customer gave with it
Peppol Response Sent on a vendor bill: the last response you sent to the supplier

Accounting users see these badges without any EDI group. Members of the EDI groups also get a Peppol Messages tab listing every message of the document — the e-invoice, responses received and sent — and each message links back through Peppol Document.

What Sent and Done prove depends on the access point. With ePošťák, Sent is acceptance for transport and Done is delivery to the recipient's access point — see delivery status.

Receiving e-invoices

The provider collects documents addressed to your Peppol address (see receiving for the common steps). For a Peppol invoice or credit note:

  • a draft vendor bill is created — a credit note becomes a vendor credit note — in the Peppol Purchase Journal, or the company's first purchase journal, using Odoo's standard UBL import for the supplier, lines, taxes and amounts;
  • the XML file is attached to the bill;
  • the bill is never posted automatically; check it like any other bill;
  • the supplier is recognised by its Peppol endpoint, and the message moves to Done. If the bill cannot be created, the message moves to Error and keeps the file; fix the cause and press Reprocess.

A document already received is skipped (and acknowledged, so the provider stops delivering it) only when its number, its kind (invoice, credit note, response), its sender's endpoint and its receiver's endpoint all match a stored message. Two suppliers' invoices with the same number, an invoice and a credit note sharing a number, or one supplier's invoices to two of your companies are therefore separate documents. A document whose sender endpoint cannot be read is always stored.

Business responses

Peppol carries two kinds of response, both as an ApplicationResponse document:

  • Message level response (MLR) — technical: whether a receiving system accepted the file;
  • Invoice Response — business: what the buyer does with the invoice.

Status codes:

Code Meaning
AB Acknowledged — received
IP In process
UQ Under query — disputed, waiting for an answer
CA Conditionally accepted
AP Accepted
RE Rejected
PD Paid

Responses from your customers. An incoming response is matched to your invoice or credit note by the document number it refers to, within the same company. An MLR fills Peppol Delivery Response; an Invoice Response fills Peppol Invoice Response and Peppol Response Reason; both write a chatter line. A response that refers to a document Odoo does not know is kept as a message, marked done, and linked to nothing.

Your response to a supplier. On a vendor bill that arrived through Peppol (both parties having a Peppol address), Peppol Response… opens a dialog:

Field Purpose
Response the status code above; defaults to Rejected
Reasons coded reasons, e.g. PRI — Prices incorrect, QTY — Quantity incorrect, REF — References incorrect
Requested actions what the supplier should do, e.g. NCR — Issue a credit note, NIN — Issue a new invoice, PIN — Provide additional information
Note free text sent to the supplier

A reason or a note is required for Rejected, Under query and Conditionally accepted. The response is sent through the provider, the bill shows Peppol Response Sent, and the chatter records it. Nothing is sent back automatically — no response is generated when you post or pay a bill.

Limitations

  • A received document whose sender endpoint cannot be read is stored each time the provider delivers it, so a re-delivery of it appears as a second message.
  • The Slovak-mandate rule is an approximation (see routing).
  • Only customer invoices and credit notes are sent. Received e-invoices become drafts; Odoo does not answer them with an MLR.
  • One Peppol transport serves the whole database; it cannot differ by company.
